primitives.name: Calibrated Edge Doctrine
primitives.verbatim_quote: **The doctrine is one rule: fire and rank on calibrated edge `e = p - q`, never on confidence `kappa = max(p, 1-p)`.** The handoff states it verbatim: "A 90%-confident favorite has ~0 edge because the line already prices it.
primitives.assumptions: Model assumes deterministic factor scoring and fixed market pricing structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p approaches q, edge vanishes, signaling no actionable information.

layer2.mapping: GSE ranks picks by e = p - q; GSI computes uncertainty bounds via conformal inference on edge residuals.
layer2.telemetry: Edge distribution variance across picks indicates model calibration quality.

primitives.name: Confidence Gating Failure
primitives.verbatim_quote: Confidence-gating = betting chalk at -EV = scores24's fatal error.
primitives.assumptions: Selection based on kappa introduces systematic bias toward low-entropy outcomes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when kappa > 0.5 but p < q, leading to negative expected value.

layer2.mapping: GSE avoids kappa-based selection; GSI models this as a misalignment between confidence and true edge.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of chalk bets with negative EV signals confidence gating artifact.

primitives.name: Market De-Vigged Probability
primitives.verbatim_quote: The repo's own edge-lab note carries the closed-form version: a published probability `(1-alpha)*p + alpha*q` leaves residual edge `(1-alpha)(p-q)`, so alpha = 0.90 keeps 10% of the independent gap, which is why GSE fires on `e = p - q` and never on a re-anchored probability (Sports/packages/prediction-engine/src/edge-lab/market-consensus-q.ts:4-11).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'alpha': 'scalar weight parameter', 'p': 'market-anchored probability', 'q': 'reference model probability', 'e_res': 'residual edge after de-vigging'}
primitives.assumptions: De-vigging preserves relative edge while adjusting for bookmaker margin.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When alpha approaches 1, residual edge shrinks to zero, eliminating signal.

layer2.mapping: GSE uses raw edge e = p - q; GSI applies de-vigging to estimate fair odds and adjust belief accordingly.
layer2.telemetry: Deviation of reported edge from theoretical edge indicates market distortion.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that edge e = p - q provides a calibrated, actionable metric for ranking predictions, whereas confidence kappa = max(p, 1-p) is a proxy that fails under market anchoring. This doctrine arises from empirical evidence showing that high-confidence chalk bets often yield negative EV due to overpriced lines. The failure mode of confidence gating lies in its assumption that higher kappa implies better predictive power, which is false when p is already adjusted for market inefficiency. The derivation of residual edge from de-vigging shows that retaining only 10% of the original gap ensures robustness against noise while preserving signal strength. This supports a dual framework where GSE operates on edge and GSI evaluates model reliability via conformal inference on edge residuals.
